parts:
Hi, 

    I am new to Stan and recently start using rstan (2.6.0) for my work. I have worked the model below for days, but it keeps giving me errors when I try to increase the number b to more than 10. So far it may work with fewer parameters and "better" simulated data. Ultimately, I would like to use it to estimate a model with more than 40 beta. 
     I have used a lot of tips from the manual or this group to improve my model, but I don't get where it goes wrong. So, I would like to get help here. Would really appreciate any feedback. Thanks a lot.

    A hierarchical heckman selection model (tobit 2). Basically, U1 = b1 * X1 + e1, and Y1 = 1 if U1>0; Y2 will be observed if Y1=1, and Y2 = b2*X2 +e2. The two error terms e1 e2 has correlation rho. The hierarchy is captured by b_i = mu * z_i + epsilon. For simplicity, I just assume that assume the covariation matrix of b is a diagonal matrix, so there is no correlation across different b. 

   ----------Stan Code---------

data {
  int<lower=0> N;           // number of customers
  int<lower=0> M;           // total number of observations
  int<lower=0> nB1;         // number of beta in equation 1
  int<lower=0> nB2;          // number of beta in equation 2
  int<lower=0> nB;
  int<lower=0> nZ;           // number of individual demographic variables plus intercept
  int<lower=0> ID[M];        // index for the observations
  matrix[N,nZ] Z;
  matrix[M,nB1] X1;
  matrix[M,nB2] X2;
  vector[M] Y1;
  vector[M] Y2;
}
parameters {

  matrix[nB,nZ] mu;                          // prior matrix for beta
  matrix[nB,N] error_beta;                        // a trick on the variance of beta

  // cholesky_factor_corr[nB] L_Omega_beta;     // the correlation matrix of the two equations, drop this one so far for simplification 
  vector<lower=0>[nB] sigma_beta;            // the s.t.d of the second equation 

  real<lower=-1,upper=1> rho_eq;              // the correlation matrix of the two equations
  real<lower=0> sigma_eq;                    // the s.t.d of the second equation 
 
}
transformed parameters {
  
  matrix[N,nB] beta;
  // beta <- Z*mu' + (diag_pre_multiply(sigma_beta,L_Omega_beta)*error_beta)';
  beta <- Z*mu' + (diag_matrix(sigma_beta)*error_beta)';

}
model{ 

  matrix[N,nB1] beta1;
  matrix[N,nB2] beta2;

  vector[M] lp;
  vector[M] value;

  rho_eq ~ uniform(-0.5,0.5);                // correlation matrix of two equations
  sigma_eq ~ cauchy(0,2);                      // constrain it to be positive   

  //L_Omega_beta ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);       // correlation matrix of beta vector
  sigma_beta ~ cauchy(0,2);                    // s.t.d. of the covariance matrix (here cause problems)

  to_vector(mu) ~ normal(0,3); 
  to_vector(error_beta) ~ normal(0,1);

  // transform beta for two equations for each customer
  beta1 <- block(beta,1,1,N,nB1);
  beta2 <- block(beta,1,nB1+1,N,nB2);

  // calculate the likelihood, because I found that using likelihood is more stable and even faster than writing the distribution for Y
  for( m in 1:M){    
    if( Y1[m] == 0 ){
      lp[m] <- normal_cdf_log(-X1[m]*beta1[ID[m]]',0,1);
    }
    else{
      value[m] <- (X1[m]*beta1[ID[m]]'+rho_eq/sigma_eq*(Y2[m]-X2[m]*beta2[ID[m]]'))/(1-rho_eq^2)^0.5;
      lp[m] <- normal_cdf_log(value[m],0,1) - log(sigma_eq) - (Y2[m]-X2[m]*beta2[ID[m]]')^2/2/sigma_eq^2;
    }
  }

  increment_log_prob( log_sum_exp( lp ) );
}

       ----------Errors ---------

     I tried fixed some parameters and only estimated the other. The issues seem to come from 
  • sigma_eq: the variance for equation 2
  • rho_eq: the correlation of the two equation
  • sigma_beta: the variance for beta 
     As an example, one of the error says: 
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::uniform_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is nan:0, but must not be nan!
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

Error : No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

     ------------R code to simulate data ---------------
# set-up for observations
N = 100;
nT = sample(10:30,N,replace=T);
M = sum(nT);
ID = rep(1:N,nT)     # ID must go from 1 to M 

# numbers of covariates for the two equations
nB1 = 5;
nB2 = 8;
nB = nB1 + nB2;

# covariance of the two equations
rho = 0.2;
sigma = 2;
Cov = matrix(c(1,rho*sigma,rho*sigma,sigma^2),2,2);

# demographics for hete
zC = matrix(c(2,0.6,0.6,2),2,2);
Z = as.matrix(cbind(1,mvrnorm(N,c(0,0),zC)));
nZ = ncol(Z);

#  prior for beta
mu = matrix(runif(nB*nZ,-1,1),nB,);
Lambda = diag(nB);

# covariates
X1 = cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(M*(nB1-1)),,nB1-1)); 
X2 = cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(M*(nB2-1)),,nB2-1)); 

# simulate actions and preferences
visit = array(0,M);
spend = array(0,M);
beta = matrix(0,N,nB);
for( i in 1:N ){
  beta[i,] = mvrnorm(1, mu%*%Z[i,],Lambda);
  beta1 = beta[1:nB1];
  beta2 = beta[(nB1+1):nB];
  for( t in 1:nT[i] ){
    if( i == 1){
      ind = t;
    }else{
      ind = sum(nT[1:(i-1)]) + t; 
    }   
    error = mvrnorm(1,c(0,0),Cov);
    u_it = X1[ind,]%*%beta1 + error[1];
    if( u_it >0 ){
      visit[ind] = 1;
      spend[ind] = X2[ind,]%*%beta2 + error[2] + 
        Cov[1,2]*dnorm(X1[ind,]%*%beta1,0,1)/pnorm(X1[ind,]%*%beta1,0,1);
    }    
  }  
}

spend = array(0,M);

  beta[i,] = mvrnorm(1, mu%*%Z[i,],Lambda);

  beta2 = beta[(nB1+1):nB];

and it's not arising from user initialization.

The problem here is that the model can't find a set of
parameter values in support.

check_not_nan(function, "Random variable", y);

you don't want to have your model be a string in R),

iteration. I have no idea how this could happen, even looking through
prob/transform.hpp.

I have a problem that there's an issue with your model in addition
to the error message, but we'll need to investigate further.

I still don't know why that particular error's coming up, but I
do see that the model's posterior is very difficult.

I managed to fit it with:

fit <- stan("heckman_hete.stan",data=data_list,
iter=4000,init=0,chains=2,
control=list(adapt_gamma=0.99,stepsize=0.005));

Setting adapt_gamma=0.99 tells it to target a low step size (more
stable) in order to have a high acceptance rate and stepsize=0.005
tells it to start with a smallish step size. In general, upping
the target acceptance rate (adapt_gamma) and dropping stepsize will
result in more stable iterations.

The problem is that the effective sample size per iteration is very very
low (on the order of 1/50 to 1/1000) and the posterior intervals are very
wide. This can come from a truly hard problem or because the model is
not well identified.

In particular, the sigma_eq parameters take very wide excursions
up to values over 1000 on some chains. A strong prior on this
would probably help tame the behavior --- the Cauchy is consistent
with extreme values.
